newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader postpones Moscow flight by a day.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader postpones Moscow flight by a day.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko has postponed a trip to Moscow to a summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) by a day to Friday, an aide said on Thursday.
BELTA, the state news agency, said Lukashenko and his delegation would now arrive in Russia on March 28 and go straight to Friday's summit of the CIS, a loose grouping of 12 former Soviet republics.
"I think the president did this because of the weather," Sergei Posykhov, Lukashenko's political aide, told Reuters.
But BELTA quoted an official in Lukashenko's adminstration as saying he had postponed the trip "because of the peculiarities of today's situation in the Russian Federation".
Tens of thousands of unpaid workers staged a day of protest across Russia on Thursday.
And the airport information centre said no flights had been postponed or delayed despite occasional snowstorms.

Lukashenko is due to meet Russian President Boris Yeltsin on a separate trip to Moscow on April 2 to sign a treaty on closer ties based on a "commonwealth" of two states they agreed on the same date last year.
Lukashenko indirectly criticised Moscow on Wednesday after the Kremlin complained about treatment of its journalists working in its small former Soviet neighbour to the west.
The Belarussian foreign ministry has withdrawn the accreditation of a Russian television journalist, accusing him of bias.
